You can use relative pronouns in defining relative clauses to talk about objects as well. These pronouns say which noun you are referring to.

If you want to refer to people, you use the relative pronouns whom or that.
If you want to refer to things, you use the relative pronouns which or that.
You can also omit or leave out object relative pronoun clauses and the meaning of the sentence will be the same.

For example:
My mother, who was born in Singapore, lived most of her life abroad.
I have just seen Titanic, which is one of the most romantic movies I have ever seen.
Speaking Note: Whom is not usually used in speaking. It can sound too formal. Many people use who instead of whom even when they are referring to the object.
Another relative pronoun that you can use is whose. This is used to talk about possession and it can be used with both people and things.

The woman whose husband is a doctor is sitting over there. (the woman's husband)
The island whose beaches have pink sand is popular with tourists. (the island's beaches)

Will, Won't, Should, Shouldn't, Can to Speculate about the Present

You can use other modal verbs like should and shouldn't to make guesses about situations in the present. You can use can to express a general possibility. Will and won't are used to express something you are certain about. Remember to use the simple form of the verb (the infinitive without “to”) after these words.

When you are very sure, use will or won't. You are 100% certain.
My grandmother lives in Brazil and because of the time difference, it is 11 o'clock at night there. She will be asleep now. She won't be awake.
If all the conditions are met (if everything happens as you expect) and you assume that something is probably true, you use should or shouldn't.

It is 10:30 a.m. on Saturday morning. My friend doesn't usually sleep in on the weekends. She should be up at this time.
I am on vacation from work and have a lot of free time. It shouldn't be a problem to find the time to run a few errands and do some housework.

Should is more often used with positive events. If you want to talk about a negative event, it would be better to use will.
Because today is Christmas Eve, the mall will be quite crowded.

Can expresses a general possibility, a situation or event we know happens sometimes.
In Canada, the winter can get very cold.

If you want to talk about a more specific possibility, use could instead.
My brother could be at the library now, but I'm not sure because he said he might stay home tonight.

images.text:
Vanessa: It shouldn't be long before we get to the top of the hill ... Wow! Look at all those stars!
Michelle: What did I tell you? Aren't they just sublime? Look at the constellation over there!
Vanessa: Wow, you must really know your stuff! I don't even know what a constellation is.
Michelle: Well all credit goes to my friend whose sister taught me all this stuff. A constellation is a group of stars that form a recognizable pattern. I'll show you an example that can help you understand it better. You see that pattern over there? What do you think it is?

Vanessa: I'm not sure, but does that look like a bull?
Michele: Yes, that constellation has the pattern of a bull. That will be the constellation, Taurus.
Vanessa: Wow! That is amazing. How many constellations are there, Michelle? There should be at least a hundred of them out there.
Michelle: According to an astronomy book that I read a few weeks ago, there are around 88 constellations in the sky. Oh look there's another one! Can you guess the one that I'm pointing to?

Vanessa: That should be a scorpion.
Michelle: Yes, that's the constellation “Scorpio”. There are others like the constellation “Pisces” whose formation looks like two fishes going in two different directions. It will be somewhere over that way.
Vanessa: It won't be that one ... Oh wait, I see it. Here's another one that looks like a ladle with a long handle.
Michelle: Oh. That will be the “Ursa Minor”, the little bear, which is commonly referred to as the “Little Dipper”.
Vanessa: This is fun, Michelle. We should do this more often.
Michelle: Yes, we definitely should! It can be cloudy this time of year though.
